143	## Detailed Design
144	
145	### Core Rules
146	
147	*Conventions.* Rules are `SE-n`; formulas `D.n`; acceptance criteria `AC-SE-n`; restore reasons `SUIT_RESTORE_*`; diagnostics `suit_*`. `[PH]` marks a placeholder that is registered with a range (Tuning Knobs) and is never a fact until the pacing spike confirms it. "(provisional — X undesigned)" marks a contract with a system whose GDD does not yet exist (Interaction, Ship Section & Layout and 2D Lighting & Occlusion were formerly in flight and are now designed; their rows quote current text); "must repeat" names what that GDD has to restate (the Graph's own rule for provisional rows). "(orchestrator ruling: ...)" marks a place where two specialist proposals disagreed and the stage rulings, or failing that a stated choice, decided. The four Graph band constants appear **only by name** (`COLD_DMG_ONSET_MC`, `HEAT_DMG_ONSET_MC`, `HYPOXIA_PP`, `DECOMP_P`); Suit reads them from the registry and never restates a value (the Graph's source-lint, AC-SE-1). Every rule carries *Rule*, *Why*, *Rejected* and *Criterion*, and is tied to a pillar. Two structural tests run through all of them: **every mutator Suit publishes changes only `suit.state`**, and **every command Suit registers is `equip_tool`**.
148	
149	*Dependency status used throughout (re-checked at the round-1 revision, 2026-10-26, Glob of `design/gdd/`).* Designed: Command & Simulation Layer, Life-Support Graph, Item & Module Database, Player Controller & Input, Emitter State & Light-Exposure Query, Save/Load & Versioned Format (also Pixel-Perfect Render Pipeline & Camera and Failure & Trail, cited only). **Designed 2026-10-26 (18:38-19:34); contract current:** `interaction-system.md` (19:34; re-verified at the final advisor review, 2026-10-27), `ship-section-and-layout-data-model.md` (18:38), `2d-lighting-and-occlusion.md` (18:48). **Designed since (re-checked at the consistency pass, 2026-10-27):** Attention, Sanity & Hallucination Rules, Boarding & Salvage, HUD & Suit Layer, Ship Body & Interior Physics, Horror Entities, Perception Filter, Adaptive Audio & Tells, Web Map & Transit, Chart Table, Modular Ship Assembly and Debug Overlay (True Values); their rows quote current text where a routed ask reached this GDD. **No file:** Co-op Session & Replication (Vertical Slice B) and Failure Contract & Re-wake (Vertical Slice). Every statement below about an absent system is a requirement this GDD places on it; statements about the three designed neighbours quote their current text.
150	
151	#### Group A — Block, hook, keying, room
152	
153	**SE-1. One block, one hook.** *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix)* *Rule.* Suit registers exactly one state block, **`suit.state`** (`class SIM`, `persist true`, `persist_scope WORLD`, `scope PER_PLAYER` keyed by PlayerId, `repl_hint SHARED_SUMMARY` per SE-36, `schema_version 1`, `supported_versions [1]`, `added_in_format 1`, `restore_after []`), and exactly one step hook, **`suit.vitals`** — divisor 6, **offset 2** (equal to `graph.propagate.atmo` under the Graph's baseline stagger, LS-8: power 0, atmo 2, failure 4), `after: [graph.propagate.atmo]` and nothing else. It never declares `after: emitter.place`. Registration is frozen at boot (CR-6): an unknown `after` id or a cycle fails boot, and there is no alias concept. The hook chain the Controller depends on is `suit.vitals` → `controller.step` → `body.integrate` → `emitter.place`; `controller.step` declares `after: suit.vitals`, `emitter.place` declares `after: [body.integrate, graph.propagate.failure]`, so Suit's own declaration is the single edge to the Graph. `restore_after` is empty because `post_restore` runs after all blocks restore (CR-8), so the `carry_ref` invariant check (SE-13) needs no restore ordering. The Graph's baseline stagger is adopted for the MVP (Graph LS-8); Suit's registration is (6, 2) and moves with `graph.propagate.atmo` by a data change, in either direction (A12 compares offsets, not values). *(The kernel's example "Suit (6, 4)" is a boot-warning fixture for never-co-running hooks, not Suit's registration; the kernel calls a same-offset pair "normal" and the Graph fixes its hooks at (6,0)/(6,2)/(6,4). The provisional block name `vitals.state` in the Controller and Save/Load drafts is replaced by `suit.state`; the sweep is a consistency-pass item, Cross-References.)* *Why.* Every designed block is `<owner>.state` and the kernel's velocity rule wants one coarse block per domain system; offset 2 gives Suit the Graph's same-tick atmosphere (atmo commits at T mod 6 = 2); offset 0 would read the previous step's atmosphere and offset 4 a value two ticks old on the failure tick. *Rejected.* Two blocks (`vitals` and `loadout`) — violates the velocity rule; offsets 0 and 4; `after: emitter.place` — creates a cycle through the Controller. *Criterion.* AC-SE-2 (hook-order list) and AC-SE-3 (boot with an unknown `after` fails). *Pillar.* P1 — the body reads the true same-tick room.
154	
155	**SE-2. Seats are keyed by PlayerId.** *Rule.* Every per-seat field lives inside dictionaries keyed by PlayerId (an int). No `peer_id`, node path or engine object appears in the block; the persistent keys are PlayerId and the item `def_id` only. *Why.* Peer ids are reassigned per connection and the kernel corrects the index's "keyed by peer ID" wording; seat identity must survive a rejoin and a restore. *Rejected.* Peer-keyed records. *Criterion.* AC-SE-4 (schema lint: no key shaped like a peer id; snapshot round-trip with a re-bound peer). *Pillar.* Serves the co-op seam (VS-B) without building it.
156	
157	**SE-3. A seat's compartment.** *Rule.* Each run, for each bound seat that is not DEAD, Suit resolves the occupant's compartment: it reads the seat's `(section_id, pos_px)` from Ship Body's read view (`section_id` from `actor_section(actor_id)`, BDY-29, derived on demand), as of T-1 (`suit.vitals` runs before `body.integrate`, so the position is up to one tick stale plus the hook's own up-to-five-tick cadence), calls Layout's pure read **`room_at(section_id, px) -> room_id | NONE`**, then the Graph's `compartment_at(room_ref)` and `compartment(cid)` for the band enums `band_o2`, `band_p`, `band_t` and the raw temperature `T`. Suit keys every cue off the **enums** (hysteresis is inherited from the Graph's `atmosphere_derive`); the raw `T` is read only for the warmth integrator's shifted-onset comparison (SE-20), against the registry names. *(orchestrator ruling: Layout's signature is adopted. The stage ruling R28 proposed a body-id form `room_at(body_id, pos_px)`; Layout's designed text publishes `room_at(section_id, px)`, so Suit takes Layout's form and Ship Body must supply `section_id`.)* **The last known room** (persisted as `last_section_id` and `last_room_ref`) **is kept for diagnostics and schema stability only; no rule reads it** (the pod needed it only for the former hold, reversed by D60, *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)*). Layout's designed text says (LY-5): "the **sill** … is not a tile and does not count in `V`: each door declares a `sill_room` … and `room_at(section_id, px)` answers `sill_room` for a px on the sill, so there is no walkable point in a section where `room_at` answers `NONE`." A NONE therefore never occurs at a walkable point inside a section; on a Layout body it is a defect-only state (Ship Body BDY-29: CI asserts it never occurs in a clean build). A seat with no room at spawn is an authoring lint failure, not a runtime state. **Two cases, keyed on the Controller's `loco_state`:** (i) **`loco_state` IN_POD**, whatever `room_at` answers (NONE, or a room of the pod's section) — **POD_RUN** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)*: statuses run (Resolved 2026-10-27 — user ruling (design-review decisions): statuses run in the pod; a death in the pod is the Controller's DEAD). The pod's Graph section is dormant and never breathed (Web Map & Transit WM-5, WM-17), so Suit calls **no `draw_air`** (M15 on a dormant section returns 0 and would raise `breath_starved`) and evaluates the seat against the **pod cabin rule**: `band_o2` ANOXIC and `band_p` NORMAL (an unbreathable pair by D.1, so the source is RESERVE and then NONE, never ROOM and never GASP), `band_t` COMFORT with no gain (`e` = 0, so no raw `T` is read and the thermal load relaxes at `TL_RELAX_COMFORT`), and the compartment id `POD_CID` (a pseudo-id distinct from NONE and from every Graph id); `o2_pp_dkpa` (the suit-sensed `p_o2`, SE-30) reads 0 in the pod, as it does for an EXPOSED seat (the suit senses no breathable O2, and the reading hue rule shows Graphite lit). The reserve drains, the cell drains while the beam is lit, the thermal load and every hold advance and the ladders step exactly as in any room (SE-35; the worked cost of a leg is in D.1). The pod is a leg's worth of transport, not a safe room. *(The cabin bands are this GDD's rule for a dormant section; Web Map & Transit and Derelict Authoring must repeat them, routed.)*; (ii) **`room_at` answers NONE with `loco_state` not IN_POD** — **EXPOSED**: the seat is exposed to the EXTERIOR (vacuum, cold), **never to the last room's bands**; by rule the air class is unbreathable with `band_p` VACUUM, `band_o2` ANOXIC and `o2_pp_dkpa` 0 *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)* (source RESERVE while the reserve lasts, then NONE; no `draw_air`), and the warmth integrator reads the Graph's EXTERIOR ambient `T_AMB_MC` (LS-3) as its raw `T`, with the `band_t` that `atmosphere_derive` gives it; everything keeps running. *(Ship Body's must-repeat, BDY-16 and BDY-29, CD-GDD-ALIGN: a body standing outside the hull must not breathe the hull's air (P1). Web Map's ASK-S1 wording ("`room_at` answers NONE **or** `loco_state == IN_POD`") is applied together with Body's ruling: IN_POD held the seat until the 2026-10-27 user ruling D60 reversed it: IN_POD now runs (POD_RUN); a bare NONE is EXPOSED. The EXTERIOR values are taken by rule from LS-3; whether `compartment(cid)` is readable on the EXTERIOR node is a routed Graph confirmation, OQ-12 (e).)* *Why.* Room polygons are Layout's and atmosphere is the Graph's; Suit owns neither. *Rejected.* Suit keeping its own room polygons; sampling a light level to decide "room". *Criterion.* AC-SE-5 (a seat on a sill takes the bands of `sill_room`; a seat that crosses a door changes bands within one run; a NONE with `loco_state` not IN_POD is EXPOSED to the EXTERIOR; an IN_POD seat runs against the pod cabin rule) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)*. *Pillar.* P1. *(Layout's designed text publishes `room_at(section_id, px)` as used here; Ship Body supplies `section_id` through `actor_section` (BDY-29); the pod is a dormant Graph section, never breathed (WM-17).)*
158	
159	#### Group B — Breath, reserve, top-up
160	
161	**SE-4. Breath source is a pure function of band enums, the reserve and the room.** *Rule.* Each run each seat picks its **breath source** from the enums of the occupant's compartment and its reserve — never from a grant that came back:
162	
163	| Air class (from the enums) | Reserve | Source | What Suit does | Breath-axis target (SE-19) |
164	|---|---|---|---|---|
165	| **AIR_OK**: `band_o2` not in {HYPOXIC, ANOXIC} **and** `band_p` not in {DECOMP, VACUUM} | any | **ROOM** | calls Graph `draw_air(cid, R_BREATH)` (M15, Class B) for the seat | by the band (OK, or STRAINED for THIN / LOW) |
166	| **Unbreathable** (the complement) | above 0 | **RESERVE** | debits `min(R_BREATH, reserve)` from the reserve; calls nothing | STRAINED, or CRITICAL at or below `RESERVE_WARN_MGU` |
167	| Unbreathable, `band_o2` HYPOXIC and `band_p` in {NORMAL, LOW} | 0 | **GASP** | calls `draw_air(cid, R_BREATH)` — whatever the room still holds | CRITICAL (never FAILED) |
168	| Unbreathable, any other combination (ANOXIC, DECOMP, VACUUM) | 0 | **NONE** | nothing is breathed | terminal condition (FAILED after the hold) |
169	
170	Because the HYPOXIC and DECOMP boundaries *are* `HYPOXIA_PP` and `DECOMP_P`, this rule uses the four named constants only through the enums, and no numeric literal of a band value appears in Suit (the Graph's source-lint passes by construction). The source is a function of enums and the reserve only: the 0.1 s lag of the Graph's queued grant (SE-5) can never open a window in which a seat is on room air, granted nothing, and not yet on the reserve. *(checkpoint ruling CK-1, 2026-10-26: GASP accepted as the single departure from R4/R14 — HYPOXIC is the Graph's "stamina loss" band and ANOXIC its "rapid incapacitation" band; the source stays a pure function of the band enums and the reserve, and FAILED requires ANOXIC, DECOMP or VACUUM with an empty reserve. Logged; OQ-1.)* *Why.* P1: the room's clock is the body's clock. The Graph's survival clocks (O2-ROOM, O2-SHIP, DOOR-BREACH) stay the player's clocks; the reserve extends the retreat window by `RESERVE_S` and does not replace them. *Rejected.* (a) A sealed tank from the first breath (makes the visible O2 graph irrelevant to a suited crew); (c) a fixed non-refillable reserve (every sortie is permanent attrition on a number the player cannot restore, and it contradicts the concept's prep step "Prep (O₂, tools, suppressants)"); choosing the source from the grant (flaps on a one-run-late value). *Criterion.* AC-SE-6 (fixture sweep over the Graph's DOOR-BREACH, O2-ROOM, O2-SHIP: the reserve engages at the first run the enums say unbreathable and never earlier) and AC-SE-1 (literal lint). *Pillar.* P1, P5 (scarcity pushes inward).
171	
172	**SE-5. Respiration ledger and the one-run lag.** *Rule.* The Graph queues `draw_air` to phase 0 of the next Graph run, applied in ascending `(compartment id, crew id)` against a running balance, and returns the shortfall `request − granted` to Suit, which owns "what a lungful of nothing does". Suit stores `pending_draw_mgu` (the request just issued for ROOM or GASP, else 0). On the following run it reconciles against the Graph's published `draw_grant(crew)` (`{requested, granted}`): the grant is attributed to the breath first, `breath_granted = min(granted, pending_draw_mgu)`, and `shortfall = pending_draw_mgu − breath_granted` (the breath part only: a room that grants exactly `R_BREATH` owes the reserve nothing, whatever extra was asked, D.2) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*; it debits `min(shortfall, reserve)` from the reserve (diagnostic `suit_reserve_shortfall`); if the reserve cannot cover the shortfall it sets the one-run flag `breath_starved`, which raises the breath-axis demand to CRITICAL for that run (D.3). Seats submit in ascending PlayerId. The 0.1 s lag is accepted and stated. *Graph confirmation (answered, Life-Support Graph LS-18, M15):* `draw_air` is queued to the next Graph run's phase 0 and the grant is published as `draw_grant(crew)` → `{requested, granted}` until the following run, so the one-run lag of this rule is the real behaviour and Suit reads `draw_grant(crew).granted` on its next run. The rule would also hold if the return were synchronous, because SE-4 never uses the grant to choose the source. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* *Why.* Closes the seam without a Graph change. *Rejected.* Switching the source on the grant. *Criterion.* AC-SE-7: request 500,000 mGU against `n_o2` 300,000: granted 300,000, shortfall 200,000 debited from the reserve one run late; two seats in one room receive grants in ascending PlayerId order. *Pillar.* P1.
173	
174	**SE-6. The reserve.** *Rule.* Each seat carries `reserve_mgu` in `0..RESERVE_MAX_MGU`, with `RESERVE_MAX_MGU = RESERVE_S × (TICK_RATE / GRAPH_STEP_TICKS) × R_BREATH` — 270,000 mGU, 90 s of breathing, at the defaults (`RESERVE_S` 90 `[PH]`, range 63-240 at `RESERVE_WARN_S` 30 and the default pod legs, narrowed from 45-240 by A15 *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*). `RESERVE_WARN_MGU` is computed the same way from `RESERVE_WARN_S` `[PH]`; both are derived on read from the time knobs and `R_BREATH` and never stored, so changing `R_BREATH` keeps the felt duration (the Item DB's F-14 ladder reads `R_BREATH`). Its debits are exactly three: the engaged-reserve spend (`R_BREATH` per run while the source is RESERVE), the leak (SE-22) and the one-run-late shortfall of a room that granted less than the breath request (SE-5, diagnostic `suit_reserve_shortfall`); its credits are exactly the V7 top-up (SE-7) and, only in the dormant PASSIVE configuration, the granted part of the room-air extra (D.2). *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* Its **physical witnesses** are mandatory (P1: a stat with no witness is the hidden stat): a valve click on engage and on disengage, a breath-cadence step (SE-26), and the sight-glass drop on the Graph's O2_TANK at top-up (drawn by In-World Instruments, Lighting and the Graph's stock). `R_BREATH` **300 mGU per step per crew, range 100-600** is a Suit-owned constant: it is today a Graph placeholder ("owned by Suit & Equipment") and is registered here. *Exported to Derelict Authoring* *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review; the former bound "a traverse of at most `RESERVE_S / 2`, never reaches CRITICAL" ignored the pod legs, the return trip and the warmth axis, and would have passed a path that cannot be survived)*: the authored vacuum budget is the minimum of two clauses (D.11). **Breath:** the sortie's total unbreathable time (out and back) plus two pod legs must not reach the warn edge, `traverse_runs + 2 × N_hi(leg) <= (RESERVE_S − RESERVE_WARN_S) × RUNS_PER_S`, which exports `VACUUM_BUDGET_S` = 27 s (274 runs) at the defaults. **Warmth:** the traverse time times the room's gain stays below `TL_CRITICAL`. `RESERVE_WARN_S ≤ RESERVE_S / 2` stays (A5), and build assertion A15 couples the reserve to two legs. The pod leg draws on the same reserve (SE-35, D60): the sortie budget is the traverse plus the legs, and D.1 gives the leg's cost *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)*. *Why.* A buffer denominated in time survives a rate change; an authoring bound keeps vacuum sections a bounded, designable thing. *Rejected.* Storing seconds (loses the Graph's own unit, which the top-up draws in). *Criterion.* AC-SE-8a to 8c (the reserve never exceeds its maximum or goes negative; every fall is exactly the sum of the three debits; the felt duration survives an `R_BREATH` change). *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* *Pillar.* P1, P5.
175	
176	**SE-7. Top-up is Interaction's verb V7; Suit supplies the credit side.** *Rule.* Refilling the reserve (at a lit O2_TANK port) and the cell (at a lit BATTERY port) is a world-targeted verb, so it is **Interaction's**: its lit, reach and reason machinery are Interaction's, and Suit does not register a world-targeted command as the primary path. This GDD writes the V7 row in full so Interaction can adopt it verbatim:

180	| Command type | `top_up` (owner Interaction; origin PLAYER; `OWNED_BY_ISSUER`, `actor_source body.state`, matching Interaction V7 *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix)*; `coalesce NONE`; `max_age_ticks` 120; **not** `allowed_when_paused`) |

Resolved 2026-10-27 — user ruling (design-review decisions): V7 `top_up` joins the MVP verb list as a deliberate O2 TAP verb (an actively chosen refill is a survival decision; a passive refill is a hidden mechanism); the Graph's LS-26 verb list and Open Question 20 are amended on the Graph's side, Interaction's IA-9 `top_up` row is adopted as written, `TOPUP_MODE` is VERB and `CELL_ENABLED` is on, so the lamp cell and the Pillar 3 "go dark" lever exist at MVP. The choice is data-only in the block through one knob, `TOPUP_MODE`: **VERB** (the shipped configuration) and **PASSIVE** (a **dormant**, tested fallback that no build selects; it is kept only so that a Graph-side delay of LS-26 could never block the MVP). In PASSIVE mode (i) the reserve refills passively from breathable room air — while `band_o2` is NORMAL and the room's `p_o2` stays at or above `TOPUP_MIN_PP` `[PH]` after the draw, Suit adds a `draw_air` of `TOPUP_PASSIVE_MGU_PER_RUN` `[PH]` to its ROOM request and, one run later, credits the part of the Graph's grant above `R_BREATH` (D.2: the breath is served first, so the extra is credited only from what exceeds the breath request, and a room that grants exactly `R_BREATH` costs the reserve nothing) (the guard exists because a 270,000 mGU fill would drop a V = 8 room from its normal partial pressure to about 176 dkPa, below the THIN boundary); and (ii) the cell is disabled (`CELL_ENABLED` 0, SE-8). The passive path is dormant at MVP and is not recommended. *(Interaction's designed text adopts this row verbatim, IA-9; the Graph's LS-26 amendment is the Graph owner's side of the 2026-10-27 ruling.)* *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)* *Why.* Prep becomes a visible ritual that spends real stock; the reserve and the cell are two symmetric prep gauges. *Rejected.* A Suit-registered `top_up` command (absorbs lit/reach/reason machinery); a passive-only reserve as the default (prep is trivial and hides the ritual). *Criterion.* AC-SE-9a to 9e. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* *Pillar.* P1, P5.

194	**SE-8. The beam cell.** *Rule.* Each seat carries `cell_ticks` in `0..CELL_MAX_TICKS`, `CELL_MAX_TICKS = CELL_S × TICK_RATE` — 72,000 ticks, **1200 s** of lit beam, at the defaults (`CELL_S` 1200 `[PH]`, range 600-2400). Each run drains `GRAPH_STEP_TICKS` (6) ticks while the seat's beam `emitter.state.lit` is true **as of T-1**; at zero Suit calls `force_off(beam_id)` (E5, Class B), which lands before the same tick's `emitter.place`. `toggle_beam.validate` reads Suit's `charge(player_id)` and rejects a turn-ON at zero with `CHARGE_EMPTY` (immediate class); a turn-OFF is always accepted. **Output is constant until empty — there is no dim**: the Emitter State's EM-8 ("no brightness dial") and its Open Question 16 are answered "no"; Suit never sets `output_pm`. The up-to-five-tick over- or under-drain per toggle at divisor 6 is accepted and stated. The cell powers nothing else in the MVP. **Fallback (data-only; dormant at MVP, because `CELL_ENABLED` is 1 by the 2026-10-27 top-up ruling, OQ-2):** `CELL_ENABLED` 0 — a distinct knob, never a sentinel value of `CELL_S` (0 means an empty cell everywhere else in this GDD): the cell never drains, and `CHARGE_EMPTY` stays registered and never fires. *Adopted text (the Emitter State's EM-10 and its Interactions row, "whichever GDD lands second adopts the other's text"):* "Suit & Equipment owns charge, drain, `CHARGE_EMPTY` and the HUD 'beam and tool charge' reading. `toggle_beam.validate` reads Suit's charge view and rejects a turn-ON at zero charge with `CHARGE_EMPTY`; a turn-OFF is always accepted. The Emitter State must repeat: Suit "keeps the hook name `suit.vitals` and its `after: graph.propagate.atmo`". *Routed asks (not Suit rules).* (i) Answered 2026-10-27: the Controller adapter holds `BEAM_TOGGLE_MIN_INTERVAL_TICKS` (registry; 10 ticks, range 10-20, PC-5) between two submitted `toggle_beam`, which exceeds the six-tick (`GRAPH_STEP_TICKS`) window: any lit span of six consecutive ticks contains exactly one sample point of the divisor-6 read, so with the debounce a toggling player cannot light the beam for free between samples; without it a span of four or fewer ticks can avoid every sample (the simulation adds no strobe cooldown). 202	**SE-11. Tool roster and `equip_tool`.** *Rule.* The hand rail's tool slots are fixed: **1 `tool_cutter`, 2 `tool_welder`, 3 `tool_scanner`**; slots 4, 5 and 6 are unbound in the MVP (slot 4 was `tool_suppressant`, removed from the MVP kit by the 2026-10-27 ruling on OQ-34, Option A) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)*. Suit registers exactly one command type, **`equip_tool {slot: 1..6}`** — origin PLAYER, `actor_binding OWNED_BY_ISSUER`, `actor_source body.state` (kernel CR-7) *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix)*, `coalesce NONE`, `max_age_ticks` 120 (the Controller's discrete-verb value), payload within `MAX_PAYLOAD`; the Controller's `tool_cycle` input is resolved by the Adapter to a slot (the Adapter, not the simulation, picks "next"). `validate` (immediate class, in this order): kernel authority; **`NOT_ACTIONABLE`** in STAGGERED, DOWNED or DEAD; **`BUSY`** while carrying a module or channelling; **`EMPTY_SLOT`** for slot 4, 5 or 6 or a tool the seat does not hold *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)*. `apply` sets `equipped_slot`; equipping the already-equipped slot is an accepted no-op. **Sim swap duration 0 ticks:** `apply` sets `equipped_slot` in the tick the command is applied, and `tool_in_hand` answers the new tool from that tick; the Controller's hand animation is presentation only and gates no command (so Sanity's rung-2 scan cost `T_EQUIP`, D.7, is exactly 0 ticks, OQ-SN-6); no noise; **never `allowed_when_paused`** (SE-32). The hand rail also shows the glowstick count and the carried module as passive entries (SE-30). *(Interaction's designed command table lists `equip_tool` as Suit's only command and registers no `use_item` (AC-IA-1); `use_item` is routed to the kernel and Item DB owners as a stale token. A use verb that acts on the world is Interaction's and calls Suit's `consume_charge`; the suppressant's effect is Attention's and Horror's and returns with the item at Vertical Slice.)* *Why.* A tool slot is a Suit fact; what a tool does is the system it acts on. *Rejected.* A holster slot 0 (no MVP verb needs a holstered state; bare-hand verbs declare no tool requirement — Interaction's); equip time (a tell-window exploit in either direction); auto-equip on target (removes a Suit decision and makes `equip_tool` pointless). *Criterion.* AC-SE-13: `equip_tool` on a carrying seat answers `BUSY`; slot 5 answers `EMPTY_SLOT`; while paused it is rejected. *Pillar.* P2 (no equipping with time stopped mid-tell), anti-pillar not a combat game (a slot, not a loadout screen).

Holder model.** *Rule.* Suit owns the three holder classes defined by the Item DB (IDB-16 "the Item DB defines what a thing is; the holder owns who has it and how many"): **HAND** (tool instances — unique per player, one of each `tool_*`, `stack_max` 1), **STOWED** (counted entries in the block, one stack per `def_id`, merged per IDB-15 when `def_id`, `condition_bp` and `charge` are equal), and **CARRIED** (the single carried instance — the Controller owns `carry_ref`, Suit owns the instance and the stored `carried_id`). All modules and the curio are CARRIED; tools are HAND; parts and glowsticks are STOWED. A refused merge leaves the surplus where it was ("the merge is refused by the holder (Suit) and the surplus stays where it was"). The persisted, hashed and replicated form of every instance Suit holds is the Item DB's positional array from `to_array()` = [def_id, count, condition_bp, cap_bp, patched_at_step, charge] (always six elements, every number an int, canonical zeros), decoded only by `from_array(a, graph_step_no)`; Suit never hand-builds an instance Dictionary *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix: Item DB IDB-15, registry `item_instance_to_array`; Suit adopts the owner's published canonical form)*; masses and classes are looked up from the static catalogue and never saved. **Suit mints no ids**: the only id it stores is the carried one, passed in by `set_carried`; stowed stacks carry no ids. There is no pack capacity and no weight limit — the carrying cost is the mass cue (SE-28) and, for a carried module, the Controller's `V_CARRY` (no run). *Why.* One owner for "who holds what"; a pack grid or weight cap is an inventory screen by another name (Item DB OQ 6). *Rejected.* A pack grid or total-weight cap. *Criterion.* AC-SE-14: a merge-and-refuse table test over `part_hull_plate` (×1), `part_duct_coupling` (×4) and `cons_glowstick` (×4). *Pillar.* P5, anti-pillar no inventory.

The carried instance and the one mover.** *Rule.* `set_carried(player_id, instance_id, instance)` stores the instance; `release_carried(player_id)` removes it and returns `(instance_id, instance)`, where `instance` is the six-element `to_array()` array of SE-12, stored and returned with every element unchanged (the identity rule, so the Interaction launder fix holds end to end) *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix)*. **Suit never self-releases.** On `locomotion_cap` NONE the Controller clears `carry_ref` and **Interaction** converts it to a loose item next tick by calling `release_carried`. Stagger does not drop the module; downed does. `post_restore` checks `controller.state.carry_ref == suit.state.carried_id` (or both NONE) and fails `SUIT_RESTORE_CARRY_MISMATCH` otherwise. The loose-world owner and the instance-id counter are not Suit's: Interaction's designed IA-28 owns `loose[]` and the id counter in `interaction.state`; Suit stores only the id it is handed, and its text holds under any owner. *Why.* Exactly one mover prevents a module existing in two holders at once. *Rejected.* Suit allocating ids (two allocators collide). *Criterion.* AC-SE-15: a carry dropped on DOWNED round-trips to a loose item with identical instance fields; a restore with a mismatched `carry_ref` fails with the named reason. *Pillar.* P1 (the world holds each thing once).

212	#### Group E — The vitals ladder, tells and death
213	
214	**SE-16. Three axes, four rungs, one cap.** *Rule.* Suit tracks three independent axes — **breath, warmth, integrity** — each at rung OK 0, STRAINED 1, CRITICAL 2 or FAILED 3. `vitals_state` is the worst axis. `locomotion_cap` is FULL for OK and STRAINED, WALK_ONLY for CRITICAL, NONE for FAILED, **derived on read and never saved**. The Controller reads exactly two Suit values: `locomotion_cap` and, since the D18 ruling, the bool read view `stowed_heavy(player_id)` (its lint allows those two names and no other Suit field; the Controller's text uses the same name `stowed_heavy`) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*. *Why.* Three physical sources, three witnesses; a worst-axis cap keeps the Controller's contract to one enum. *Rejected.* One scalar "health" (a hidden stat, P1); band-entry-only states (kills inside the Graph's DOOR-BREACH window with no tell). *Criterion.* AC-SE-18: a cap-mapping table test; the Controller source references no other Suit field. *Pillar.* P1, P2.
215	
216	**SE-17. An axis climbs one rung per qualifying hold; descent is never rate-limited (`vitals_ladder_step`).** *Rule.* For the two **counter axes** (breath, integrity) each run evaluates a **demand** `d` in 0..2 and a **terminal condition** `t` from the true state (SE-19, SE-22). With `r` the current rung: (1) if `r ≤ 2` and `d < r`, the rung drops to `d` **immediately** (any distance) and the hold resets; (2) if `r = 0` and `d ≥ 1`, the rung becomes 1 **immediately** — the first cue fires as early as the true state allows; (3) if `r = 1` and `d ≥ 2`, a hold counter increments and the rung becomes 2 when it reaches `HOLD_12 = ceil(RUNG_MIN_TICKS / GRAPH_STEP_TICKS)` runs (100 runs = 10 s at `RUNG_MIN_TICKS` **600**); (4) if `r = 2` and `t`, a hold counter increments and the rung becomes 3 when it reaches `HOLD_23(axis)` runs (breath: `max(HOLD_12, HYPOX_FAIL_S × (TICK_RATE / GRAPH_STEP_TICKS))`, 150 runs = 15 s at `HYPOX_FAIL_S` 15 `[PH]`; integrity: `max(HOLD_12, INTEG_FAIL_S × (TICK_RATE / GRAPH_STEP_TICKS))`, 100 runs at `INTEG_FAIL_S` 10 `[PH]`; warmth: `(TL_MAX − TL_CRITICAL) / TL_GAIN_MAX`, 200 runs, SE-20); (5) if `r = 3`, it stays 3 while `t` holds and drops to `min(d, 2)` on the run `t` clears; (6) every promotion, demotion and every run in which the qualifying condition does not hold resets the hold to 0 — **a blip resets the counter**, so a two-second DECOMP transient never climbs past STRAINED. Mass never changes speed or noise (there is no continuous term; the one discrete exception is the Controller's rule D18, ruled 2026-10-27: **run is disabled while any HEAVY item is stowed**, with no grams term, `V_CARRY` and `NOISE_PER_TICK` unchanged; Suit supplies the read `stowed_heavy`, SE-40) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)*. *(Boarding & Salvage and Sanity must repeat: the VS-A field check on a carried item is valid only while the stowed class is below the carried class under test — drop the plate first; the knob `STOWED_CUE_FLOOR_CLASS` and this precondition are OQ-8, ruled at checkpoint CK-8.)* *Rejected carriers.* Shiver (cold), visor fog (bad air), a vignette (SE-27), pack-breathing amplitude (not on the closed list). *Risk RK-2 stands:* a blind two-clip audio test (load versus thin air, at least 90 % identification) is a precondition for the Vertical Slice A phantom-salvage check; the MVP exposure is the plate and a carried module. *Criterion.* AC-SE-29 (the D.6 table; the manual blind audio test, a spike). *Pillar.* P1, P4.
253	
254	**SE-29. Readings versus cues; lie-capable architecture, honest MVP.** *Rule.* Every HR-3 reading reaches the HUD only through the Perception Filter's **`perceived`**, which wraps **`true_value(key, player_id)`**, with keys **`suit.o2`, `suit.reserve`, `suit.integrity`, `suit.warmth`, `suit.charge`** (the five lie-capable readings; the sixth key, `suit.alarm`, is a TRUTH-class bit, below) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)*. The architecture is lie-capable (the reading is drawn in the reading register with the art bible's HR-5 tri-modal tell), but **no reading is corrupted in the MVP** — the MVP's single class (b) hallucination lives on ship instruments. Body cues are never corruptible regardless. A lying numeral is disproved by a crewmate's visor or by breath cadence, the costly check; Pillar 2 protects a first-time player's only death clock until the cue ladder is playtested. The glowstick count beside its rail glyph is an **anchor**, not a reading: honest at MVP and Vertical Slice A, with no `true_value` key (HUD HS-34, Sanity SN-19; OQ-6 closed; the suppressant count left the MVP rail, OQ-34). **`suit.alarm`** (OQ-37, Resolved 2026-10-27 — user ruling (design-review decisions): accepted at MVP) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)*: a sixth `true_value` key, a one-bit **TRUTH-class** reading derived inside Suit: `alarm_bit` is 1 iff the Graph's published pure read `alarm_sections()` (LS-13 (c)) intersects `sections_of(body_of(section_id))`, where `section_id` is the seat's section already resolved at SE-3 (`actor_section`) and `body_of` / `sections_of` are Layout's pure reads: the seat's loop set is all six loops (0..5, compartment descriptors included) of every section of the body the seat stands on, the same predicate as the Graph annunciator's listener scope (Audio AA-27), so the mark is lit exactly when a klaxon is audible to that seat. A seat with no section, or DEAD, reads 0. A derelict breach or a thin/decompressed derelict room is in the loop set; the bit is gated by the Graph's 100-step fairness window (D.11), so on the DOOR-BREACH fixture it first reads 1 at step 125 (ATMO_THIN, Graph D.11 Example B) *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix)*. The Perception Filter wraps it as a TRUTH-class key: **never lie-capable** (it carries no HR-5 lie slots and Sanity may not corrupt it), never naming a loop or a place, derived on read from the last committed Graph state and never saved. It gives a deaf or hard-of-hearing player under reduced motion a ship-alarm tell (Pillar 2), it is the sixth mark slot (SE-30), and it is a fact about the ship, not an Attention indicator (AC-SE-93). **The warmth reading's value.** `true_value(suit.warmth, player_id)` is a cold-to-hot permille of the thermal load, `warmth_pm = (500 × (thermal_load + TL_MAX)) / TL_MAX` (integer division of a non-negative numerator; 0..1000; COMFORT, `thermal_load` 0, at the centre 500; cold below), carried by the Filter as the `Perceived` displayed permille; it is a load, not a body temperature (no temperature number exists, SE-20). Its six band edges are the images of −`TL_MAX`, −`TL_CRITICAL`, −`TL_STRAINED`, +`TL_STRAINED`, +`TL_CRITICAL`, +`TL_MAX`: **0, 333, 466, 533, 666, 1000** at the defaults `[PH]`, so the zone band matches the load thresholds of the warmth rung (SE-20); a band-driven STRAINED (FROST with no load yet) leaves the reading in its centre zone — the body is ahead of the number (Player Fantasy). The HUD's equal spacing is replaced by these edges (HUD & Suit Layer OQ-HS-9). Must be repeated by the HUD & Suit Layer, Sanity & Hallucination Rules and the Perception Filter. *Rejected.* Corrupted-in-MVP (a lying O2 numeral on an untested death clock); never lie-capable (loses the "my numeral says warm, my visor is fogged" teaching moment). *Criterion.* AC-SE-30: a stub Filter wrapping `true_value` changes the HUD value and no body cue. *Pillar.* P4, P2.
255	
256	**SE-30. The O2 numeral, the reserve reading and the hand rail.** *Rule.* *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review: when the reserve engages it becomes the death clock, but it sat on the corner panel while the strip kept showing a room `p_o2` of 0 in cyan with the player breathing fine, and the breath warning mark changed position with the breath source.)* The two O2 readings are named **ambient O2** (`suit.o2`: the **suit-sensed `p_o2` (dkPa) of the occupant's compartment** — "the suit's reading of compartment atmosphere via Suit, not a Graph overlay") and **suit O2** (`suit.reserve`, a fill fraction in permille of `RESERVE_MAX_MGU`, `reserve_pm` 0..1000; never seconds, because a seconds readout jumps when the leak starts; the HUD chooses how the fraction is drawn; it has its own glyph on the suit panel) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review, delegated ruling R8)*. **The critical strip's breath dial (arc and numeral) shows the suit O2 while the breath source is RESERVE, and the ambient O2 in every other source**; while it shows the suit O2 the ambient numeral is demoted to the suit panel (the HUD places it, OQ-41). **Each axis has one mark anchor:** the breath axis's warning mark always sits on the strip's breath dial when the breath axis is CRITICAL, whichever reading the dial is showing and whichever the breath source is (GASP, NONE or RESERVE); it no longer moves between the reserve glyph and the O2 reading. This adds a reading to HR-3's set — an art-bible amendment routed to the art-director (accepted by the art-director; amendment text owed). **The mark is rung-based, not condition-based**: it fires only at the CRITICAL rung of an axis (after the hold, so a transient never shows it) and at `CELL_WARN_S` on the charge reading, never at STRAINED; this keeps it rare. **Per-rung marks and six slots** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)* (HUD HS-65 confirmed by the user; OQ-37 ruled): each mark is keyed to its own Suit rung. The strip mark shows whenever the breath rung is CRITICAL, and the reserve glyph's mark additionally shows while `mark_reserve` is true (D.10: `rung_breath >= 2 and breath_src == RESERVE`, derived on read with no new state; the HUD's HS-65 draws it) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*, so up to five rung or charge marks can coexist (strip, reserve, warmth, integrity, charge); the one-bit `suit.alarm` adds a **sixth** mark slot, which is not rung-based: it shows while the bit is 1 and sits beside no reading. This supersedes the single breath anchor above for the case of an engaged reserve. **The maximum visible mark count is six, stated once here** (five rung or charge marks plus the alarm); the strip mark and the reserve mark are two marks on one breath fact, and whether the panel's reserve entry is merged into the strip or hidden while the dial already shows the suit O2 (which would remove the duplicate beacon) is the HUD's decision, OQ-41 (b); either way the count never exceeds six *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*. The mark inherits the class of the reading it sits beside — it lies when the reading lies and is **not** an independent honest backup; the honest second opinion is always the body and the room. **Hand rail** (the Item DB's OQ 6 confirmed): the three MVP tools, the glowstick count 0-4, the carried-module glyph, and the equipped tool in the Tungsten fixture colour *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)* (the suppressant left the rail, OQ-34); **no weight readout, no inventory screen, no per-part counts** (a part count is read by Interaction's repair prompt). *Criterion.* AC-SE-31 (retained screenshots; UI BLOCKING). *Pillar.* P1, P4.
257	
258	#### Group F — Seams
259	
260	**SE-31. No stimuli pushed.** *Rule.* Suit pushes no noise or power stimuli to Attention in the MVP. Per-verb noise class lives in **Interaction's verb declarations**; Suit keeps no noise field of its own (the earlier idea of a Suit-side noise table is withdrawn so there is one table of record). The kernel's Interactions row 4 says Suit "pushes noise/power stimuli to Attention": that wording is a routed refresh (Cross-References). The top-up is a Graph stock withdrawal; whether Attention sees it is not relied on here. *Criterion.* AC-SE-32 (no call from Suit's code to an Attention intake). *Pillar.* P3.
261	
262	**SE-32. Pause.** *Rule.* Nothing Suit registers carries `allowed_when_paused`; `equip_tool` and every mutator are rejected while paused. The Chart Table's beam-shape pick is a boot or new-game call, not a runtime command. *Rejected.* Paused equip (lets a solo player re-arm with time stopped mid-tell, against Pillar 2). *Criterion.* AC-SE-33. *Pillar.* P2.
263	
264	**SE-33. Autosave seam (adopted: Save/Load's package).** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)* *Rule.* Resolved 2026-10-27 — user ruling (design-review decisions): accept Save/Load's package (OQ-13; Save/Load OQ-40 and OQ-41; D14 and D42): (a) "any bound seat `vitals_state ≥ CRITICAL`" is a **third soft-gate input** for the autosave (deferred up to `AUTOSAVE_MAX_DEFER_TICKS`, registry 7200, then written RISKY, invisible to the player: no glyph) and is **also applied to `quit_risky`**; (b) a **fairness step-back**: `loop_hit` also fires when `T_downed − g_r.T < W_MIN_WARNING_S × TICK_RATE`, independent of `risky`; (c) a **post-DOWNED refractory** of `W_MIN_WARNING_S × TICK_RATE` ticks. Save/Load owns (a)-(c) and their draft criteria AC-SL-128 and AC-SL-129, which are promoted there. *Suit's half.* Suit supplies exactly one input, `view(player_id).vitals_state` (the worst of the three persisted rungs, derived on read, never saved), and changes nothing else; a derived `time_to_failure_runs` read is **not minted** (a STRAINED-yet-doomed seat, for example 31 s of reserve and a 40 s exit, is caught by the step-back (b), not by the gate). *Derivation of the window used by (b) and (c).* `W_MIN_WARNING_S` is the registry's 10 s and `TICK_RATE` is 60, so the window is 10 × 60 = **600 ticks**. It is the Graph's own fairness floor, and Suit's `SUIT_MIN_WARNING_S` (20 s, 1,200 ticks) is at least twice it (build assertion A1). A generation written inside the final 600 ticks before a DOWNED seat's `T_downed` would restore the player with less than the minimum warning, so the step-back skips it. *Worked example.* A seat is first cued at tick t0 and is DOWNED at t0 + 1,500 (25 s, the breath floor of D.11): an autosave written at t0 + 1,000 is 500 ticks before `T_downed`, inside the window, so `loop_hit` fires and the restore steps back past it; one written at t0 + 800 is 700 ticks before and is not stepped back. The second route into a doomed restore, a data retune making every saved restore fail, is closed on Suit's side by `data_rev` (SE-34, AC-SE-49). The event autosaves for weld, cut and module-cut (D17), the assembly-breach withholding (D54) and the fault loss window (D55) are Save/Load's and Assembly's. *Criterion.* AC-SE-34a and 34b. *Pillar.* P5.
265	
266	**SE-34. Save, restore, derived values.** *Rule.* SL-15 items 1-12 apply: `supported_versions`; a plain-data `snapshot()` (no `Vector2i`, no `StringName` keys, no typed containers); a two-phase `restore` returning `(ok, reason, detail)`; **hard failure, never clamp** on an out-of-range field *(except the declared `data_rev` migration below)*; `default_state()`; `post_restore` sets every `prev_*` field to its current value (no spurious edge cue after a restore); explicit dirty keys (4.7 packed-array rule); restore-idempotent (`snapshot(restore(snapshot()))` byte-equal); PER_PLAYER keyed by PlayerId. The closed restore reasons are in SE-38. **Data revisions** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*: the block persists a block-level `data_rev` (the revision of `assets/data/suit/*.json`, bumped by hand for any retune of `R_BREATH`, `RESERVE_S`, `CELL_S`, `TL_MAX`, `RUNG_MIN_TICKS`, `HYPOX_FAIL_S`, `INTEG_FAIL_S` or `STAGGER_WINDOW_TICKS`), and `assets/data/suit/rev_history.json` keeps, for each past revision, the saved values of `R_BREATH`, `RESERVE_S`, `CELL_S`, `TL_MAX` and the derived hold maxima. A saved `data_rev` equal to the current one is restored strictly (an out-of-range field is `SUIT_RESTORE_FIELD_RANGE`, a defect or tampering). A saved `data_rev` **older** than the current and present in the history is a legitimate retune and is **rescaled, not failed**: `reserve_mgu` and `cell_ticks` keep their felt fraction (`new = floor(saved × RESERVE_MAX_now / RESERVE_MAX_saved)`, likewise `CELL_MAX_TICKS`), `thermal_load` and every `hold`, `rf_warmth` and `p_age` are reduced to the new maxima (the safe direction: a shorter counter only lengthens the tell), the diagnostic `suit_restore_rescaled` is emitted, and the restore succeeds. A saved `data_rev` newer than the build, or absent from the history, fails `SUIT_RESTORE_DATA_REV_UNKNOWN`. Without this path a data retune made every saved restore fail and left the player with no loadable save at the moment of death (the doomed-save risk of OQ-13's second route). The rescale is a declared migration, not a clamp; Save/Load confirms it is within SL-15 (OQ-45). **Instance decode** *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix)*: in `post_restore` (the same place and mechanism as `SUIT_RESTORE_CARRY_MISMATCH`; Suit's `restore_after` is `[]` but `post_restore` runs after all blocks restore, CR-8) Suit decodes every held instance with `from_array(a, graph_step_no)`, `graph_step_no` being the restored Graph's absolute 10 Hz `step_no`; a wrong length or element type fails `SUIT_RESTORE_INSTANCE_FORM`, a `validate_instance` failure maps to `SUIT_RESTORE_FIELD_RANGE`, an unknown `def_id` stays `SUIT_RESTORE_UNKNOWN_DEF` and a count above `stack_max` stays `SUIT_RESTORE_STOWED_OVERFLOW`; live state is untouched and nothing is clamped. Derived values — `locomotion_cap`, `vitals_state`, cue levels, `held_mass_g`, `stowed_mass_g`, `cue_load`, the breath source — are computed on read and never saved. MVP death is restart from the last autosave: `suit.state` rolls back with the world and there is no PROFILE block in the MVP. *Criterion.* AC-SE-35 (SL-15 round trip, restore idempotence). *Pillar.* P5.
267	
268	**SE-35. External stagger, DECOMP pull, pod.** *Stagger.* The Controller registers the `SYSTEM`-origin command type `stagger {actor}` (registry `stagger`; Player Controller PC-1 b: `coalesce NONE`, `max_age_ticks` 120, no player binding, rejected `NOT_STAGGERABLE` in DOWNED, DEAD or IN_POD, Applied without extending the lock in STAGGERED); the former CONFLICT is closed, 2026-10-27. Suit submits one on a two-band pressure drop inside `STAGGER_WINDOW_TICKS` `[PH]` (dormant at MVP: no locked fixture fires it; the specified interface stays and is tested on synthetic traces; OQ-38) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*, evaluated by **D.12** (the one normative statement of the trigger): the occupant's `band_p` index (NORMAL 0, LOW 1, DECOMP 2, VACUUM 3) must rise by 2 or more between a sample taken at most `STAGGER_WINDOW_TICKS` earlier and the current run, **in the same compartment**. A compartment change (a door crossing, the SE-3 NONE-to-EXPOSED switch, leaving IN_POD, the first run after a bind) re-anchors the window and never counts, so a player who walks into a vented room by choice is not input-locked for it, while a pressure fall inside the room they stand in is; one stagger per event; the two window ages are persisted (SE-38) so a restore mid-window replays the same trigger; the DECOMP cue plays as well, and a cap falling edge still staggers through the Controller's own rule. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* *Pull.* Cue only (a lean, draught audio, dust); no displacement ("a stagger is animation plus input lock, never an impulse"). *Pod* *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)* (D60 reverses the former hold). Resolved 2026-10-27 — user ruling (design-review decisions): statuses run in the pod, and a death in the pod is the Controller's DEAD. While the Controller's `loco_state` is IN_POD, Suit runs the full SE-39 sequence for the seat against the pod cabin rule of SE-3 (i) (POD_RUN): **no `draw_air` call** (the pod's section is dormant and never breathed, Web Map & Transit WM-5, WM-17); the breath source is RESERVE and then NONE; the reserve drains `R_BREATH` per run; the cell drains while the beam is lit; the thermal load relaxes against COMFORT with no gain; every hold counter advances; the cap, the cues and the marks follow the ladders as anywhere. `pending_draw_mgu` is 0 in the pod, so no shortfall can arise: `breath_starved` stays 0 and no GASP cue fires across a leg (Web Map WM-17's required criterion holds by construction). A seat that reaches FAILED in the pod is DOWNED and then DEAD by the Controller's own rule (`DOWN_TO_DEATH_TICKS`); Suit special-cases nothing and holds nothing. What a leg costs, and when it can kill, is derived in D.1 (a nominal leg of 945 ticks spends 157 runs x 300 = 47,100 mGU, 15.7 s of the 90 s reserve, with the remainder of 3 ticks carried, so 157 or 158 runs; a pod death needs a leg of at least 250 runs, 25 s, so it is unreachable at the registry defaults) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review, delegated ruling R6)*. The `stagger` trigger cannot fire in the pod (D.12: `band_p` is NORMAL there by rule, and the Controller rejects `stagger` as `NOT_STAGGERABLE` in IN_POD); what a cap falling edge does while IN_POD is the Controller's (routed). A NONE with `loco_state` not IN_POD is not the pod: it is EXPOSED to the EXTERIOR (SE-3, Ship Body BDY-29). *(Web Map & Transit WM-17 and ASK-S1 answered the former Open Question 32 with a hold; the ruling D60 reverses that answer. Resolved 2026-10-27 — delegated ruling R6 (re-review; user delegated to best judgment): Suit's RUN reading stands and Web Map conforms on its side (WM-17b's HOLD reading deleted, ASK-S2 closed); Suit does not edit Web Map and does not claim the edit is done. The valve click plays only on the source transition edge: once on entering RESERVE and once on the disengage at arrival, never per run.)* *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review, delegated ruling R6)* *Criterion.* AC-SE-36a to 36f and AC-SE-94. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review; 2026-10-27 — user rulings)* *Pillar.* P1.
269	
270	**SE-36. Co-op seams (record, do not build).** *Rule.* `repl_hint` is `SHARED_SUMMARY`, defined as exactly **`{locomotion_cap, vitals_state, cue_cold, cue_fog, cue_load, beam_shape, charge_band, carried_class}`** — no reserve value, no tool charges, no integrity number. A reading is private truth; a cue is public truth. The crew strip carries no vitals by default (the honest check is lighting a crewmate's visor). `revive` is dormant. Shape uniqueness is Co-op Session's; I-SUPPLY at four seats is SE-10's note. *Requested amendment (routed, not adopted on this GDD's authority):* the art-director finds the eight fields cannot drive all crewmate overlays — the summary lacks the seam jet (`cue_leak`) and the HEAVY back-frame (`stowed_heavy`), `cue_cold` must carry four values (none, vapour, rime level 1, rime level 2), and the systems-designer asks for a signed thermal cue so the heat side is not dropped; VS-B only (OQ-5). *Criterion.* AC-SE-37. *Pillar.* P1 (human channel).
271	
272	**SE-37. No randomness, no scene tree.** *Rule.* Suit uses no RNG, no wall clock and no `delta` (H9): drain, ladder and cue thresholds are deterministic. Suit's hook, mutators and block contain no `Node` (H10). All values are int32-safe. *Criterion.* AC-SE-38. *Pillar.* P1 (replay determinism).

277	
278	| Field | Type | Range | Persisted | Dirty key (bucket) |
279	|---|---|---|---|---|
280	| `reserve_mgu` | int | 0..`RESERVE_MAX_MGU` | yes | `S/<PlayerId>` on a 5 % bucket of the maximum, on the engage edge and the warn edge |

303	
304	One `S/<PlayerId>` dirty family per seat per change burst — never one key per field — and a restore yields one `ALL` notification then silence; the budget is well under `MAX_DIRTY_KEYS` 256. Size is on the order of 330 bytes per seat after the 2026-10-27 additions (`p_age0`, `p_age1`, `rf_warmth`, `pending_extra_mgu`, `breath_src_change_seq` and one block-level `data_rev`), under 1.5 KB at four seats *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*. The **closed restore reasons** are `SUIT_RESTORE_SCHEMA_UNSUPPORTED`, `SUIT_RESTORE_FIELD_RANGE` (any field outside the table, including a `rung` not in 0..3, a `hold` or `rf_warmth` above its maximum or a `p_age` above `STAGGER_WINDOW_RUNS` + 1), `SUIT_RESTORE_STOWED_OVERFLOW` (a count above `stack_max`), `SUIT_RESTORE_UNKNOWN_DEF`, `SUIT_RESTORE_BEAM_SHAPE`, `SUIT_RESTORE_CARRY_MISMATCH`, `SUIT_RESTORE_SEAT_UNBOUND`, `SUIT_RESTORE_DATA_REV_UNKNOWN` *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* and `SUIT_RESTORE_INSTANCE_FORM` (a held instance array of the wrong length or with a wrong element type) *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix)*. *Criterion.* AC-SE-35 and AC-SE-49a-c. *Pillar.* P5.

347	**SE-41. Suit supplies the holder side with three Class B mutators, in addition to the SE-40 table: **`reserve_stowed(player_id, def_id, n) -> bool`** (moves `n` from the stowed count to a per-seat `reserved` bucket; returns false and changes nothing if the stowed count is below `n`), **`release_stowed(player_id, def_id, n)`** (returns reserved units to the stowed count) and **`consume_reserved(player_id, def_id, n)`** (destroys reserved units — the part is spent). A part in the reserved bucket is treated as having **left the pack from the begin tick, in both truth branches**: it is excluded from `stowed_count`, from `stowed_mass_g` and therefore from `cue_load`. Physically, the reserved part is at the work site, out of the pack, from the begin tick in both truth branches — so `cue_load` and the HEAVY back-frame remain true readings of what is on the back, never a suppressed cue (P1). The ledger of RESERVED and PAID records, their absolute `until` and `grace_until` ticks and the resume allowance are **Interaction's** (persisted in its own block); Suit persists only the per-seat reserved counts (SE-38), so a restore mid-job keeps the reservation and reintroduces no oracle. `spend_stowed` remains for the glowstick throw. A pickup into a stack that has units reserved is bounded by `stack_max` over stowed plus reserved. *(Interaction's designed IA-18 carries the three names, which Suit adopts on the precedent that the second GDD adopts the first's text. The stage ruling's R20 list had only `spend_stowed` for "a part on the first productive FULL step"; the reservation supersedes that caller. Interaction's stated fallback if Suit refuses — keep the spend at the first productive step and accept a one-run oracle — is not taken.)* *Why.* P1 and P4: an oracle that answers "is this module truly damaged" for free defeats the cost rule that makes a hallucinated broken state falsifiable only by time or risk. *Rejected.* Spending at the first productive step only (the oracle); refunding on abort (a free probe). *Criterion.* AC-SE-40: reserve → read `stowed_count` and `cue_load` → both fall at the begin tick whether or not the subject is damaged; `release_stowed` and `consume_reserved` conserve the total. *Pillar.* P1, P4.

504	## Formulas
505	
506	*Conventions.* Every formula is per seat, per `suit.vitals` run (one run = `GRAPH_STEP_TICKS` ticks = one Graph step = 0.1 s; runs per second = `TICK_RATE / GRAPH_STEP_TICKS` = 10). Everything is integer arithmetic; every quotient is taken on non-negative operands (floor unless `ceil` is written), because GDScript integer division truncates toward zero and the engine reference has no scripting file to confirm a convention for negative operands (→ ADR candidate 4; NOT SOURCEABLE). Nothing here is hashed or replicated except the block, whose fields are all ints (kernel D.10 and D.12 apply). The four Graph band constants appear only as names. "Step n" in a worked example means the n-th Graph step (= Suit run) after the fixture's t = 0, counted exactly; every fixture time is `[derived; the Graph harness confirms to ±15 %]`. D.1 to D.7 are the seven formulas registered at Phase 5 (R32); D.8 to D.12 are unregistered helpers that restate derived values and build assertions. **Number provenance:** where the game-designer and systems-designer proposals diverged, the stage rulings and the already-written rules decided; the divergences are listed in Tuning Knobs and Open Questions. Every constant below is `[PH]` unless it is a registry name cited by name.
507	
508	### D.1 `suit_breath_source`
509	
510	The `suit_breath_source` formula is defined as:
511	
512	```
513	AIR_OK   = (band_o2 in {NORMAL, THIN}) AND (band_p in {NORMAL, LOW})
514	AIR_POOR = (band_o2 == HYPOXIC)        AND (band_p in {NORMAL, LOW})
515	AIR_NONE = (band_o2 == ANOXIC)         OR  (band_p in {DECOMP, VACUUM})
516	source   = ROOM    if AIR_OK
517	         = RESERVE if (AIR_POOR or AIR_NONE) and reserve_mgu > 0
518	         = GASP    if AIR_POOR and reserve_mgu == 0
519	         = NONE    if AIR_NONE and reserve_mgu == 0
520	```
521	
522	**Variables:**
523	
524	| Variable | Type | Range | Source | Description |
525	|---|---|---|---|---|
526	| `band_o2` | enum | NORMAL, THIN, HYPOXIC, ANOXIC | Graph `compartment(cid)`; ANOXIC by rule for an EXPOSED seat and for an IN_POD seat (SE-3) | the occupant's O2 band; hysteresis inherited; for an IN_POD seat the pod cabin rule supplies ANOXIC (POD_RUN, D60) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)* |
527	| `band_p` | enum | NORMAL, LOW, DECOMP, VACUUM | Graph `compartment(cid)`; VACUUM by rule for an EXPOSED seat, NORMAL by rule for an IN_POD seat (SE-3) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)* | the occupant's pressure band |
528	| `reserve_mgu` | int mGU | 0..`RESERVE_MAX_MGU` | `suit.state`, after this run's shortfall debit (D.2) | the seat's reserve |
529	| `source` | enum | ROOM, RESERVE, GASP, NONE | result | drives D.2 and the breath-axis demand (SE-19) |
530	
531	**Output Range:** exactly one of four values; total over the domain (AIR_OK takes 4 of the 16 band pairs, AIR_POOR 2, AIR_NONE 10). 555	debit_sf       = min(shortfall, reserve_mgu)
556	reserve_1      = min(RESERVE_MAX_MGU, reserve_mgu - debit_sf + extra_credit)       # the cap clamps; nothing is created

558	source         = suit_breath_source(band_o2, band_p, reserve_1)     # D.1

560	extra          = D.9 PASSIVE guard (0 unless TOPUP_MODE is PASSIVE and source == ROOM)

562	leak           = LEAK_MGU_PER_RUN if integrity_bp < SUIT_LEAK_HP else 0     # integrity as it stands at the start of the run
563	reserve_2      = reserve_1 - spend
564	reserve_mgu'   = reserve_2 - min(leak, reserve_2)

879	### D.10 `suit_cue_levels`
880	
881	The `suit_cue_levels` formula is defined as:
882	
883	```
884	cold_side = band_t in {FROST, FREEZING, DEEP_COLD} or (thermal_load < 0 and band_t not in {HOT, SCORCH})     # residual cold load never draws rime or shiver in a hot room (P1)
885	cue_cold  = 3 if cold_side and rung_warmth >= 2 ; 2 if cold_side and rung_warmth == 1 ; 1 if band_t in {COOL, FROST, FREEZING, DEEP_COLD} ; else 0     # vapour 1, shiver and rime 1 at 2, rime 2 at 3
886	cue_fog   = min(rung_breath, 2)
887	breath_step = min(rung_breath, 2)   # the pace step; the air class drives the rate, the load layers never do (SE-28)
888	cue_breath  = {src: breath_src, air_class: 0 AIR_OK / 1 AIR_POOR / 2 AIR_NONE (D.1), pace_step: breath_step}     # the primary cue's level definition: ROOM open, RESERVE closed, GASP laboured, NONE gasp loop
889	breath_src_change_seq = (breath_src_change_seq + 1) mod 65536 on each run in which breath_src differs from the previous run     # the edge counter behind the valve click, engage and disengage
890	cue_load  = D.6
891	charge_band = D.5
892	charge_advise = D.5                    # the silent advisory step on the charge reading (no audio, no mark)
893	carried_class = 0 if no carried instance else 1 + weight_class(carried instance)
894	mark_axis = (rung_axis >= 2) for breath, warmth, integrity ;  mark_charge = (charge_band == 1)                # rung-based, never at STRAINED (SE-30)
895	mark_reserve = (rung_breath >= 2 and breath_src == RESERVE)                                                       # re-review: derived on read, no new state; the per-rung mark beside the reserve glyph (SE-30), never at STRAINED
896	leak_jet = integrity_bp < SUIT_LEAK_HP ;  back_frame = stowed_cls == HEAVY
897	```

984	### D.12 `pressure_drop_stagger` *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review: added; closes the BLOCKING finding that the only live external-stagger trigger had no formula, no persisted state and no rule for compartment changes or restore)*

986	The `pressure_drop_stagger` formula is defined as:
987	
988	```
989	IDX(band_p)   = 0 NORMAL, 1 LOW, 2 DECOMP, 3 VACUUM                       # higher = lower pressure; EXPOSED seat: VACUUM (3) by rule (SE-3); IN_POD seat: NORMAL (0) by rule
990	W             = floor(STAGGER_WINDOW_TICKS / GRAPH_STEP_TICKS)             # STAGGER_WINDOW_RUNS: 60 / 6 = 10 (range 5..20)
991	SAT           = W + 1                                                      # "older than the window"
992	# per bound seat, once per run, after the room is resolved (SE-39 step 2). Not evaluated for a DEAD seat; evaluated in the pod like anywhere (D60), with `cid` = POD_CID and `band_p` NORMAL by rule, so it cannot fire there, and entering or leaving the pod changes `cid` and re-anchors *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)*.
993	p             = IDX(band_p) ;  cid = the occupant's compartment id (EXTERIOR for an EXPOSED seat)
994	if cid != prev_cid :                                                       # a crossing, the first run after a bind, entering or leaving IN_POD (cid changes to or from POD_CID)
995	    p_age0 = 0 if p == 0 else SAT ;  p_age1 = 0 if p <= 1 else SAT ;  fire = false     # re-anchor: the new room's history starts now; a crossing never counts
996	else :
997	    p_age0 = 0 if p == 0 else min(SAT, p_age0 + 1)                         # runs since the band index was 0
998	    p_age1 = 0 if p <= 1 else min(SAT, p_age1 + 1)                         # runs since the band index was 0 or 1
999	    fire   = (p == 2 and p_age0 <= W) or (p == 3 and p_age1 <= W)          # a rise of >= 2 against a sample no older than W runs (inclusive)
1000	    if fire : p_age0 = SAT ; p_age1 = SAT                                  # one stagger per event; the consumed samples cannot fire again
1001	prev_cid      = cid
1002	fire  ->  submit SYSTEM stagger {actor}   (the result, including NOT_STAGGERABLE, is ignored; never retried)
1003	```
1004	
1005	**Why two ages and not one reference.** A single stored reference band cannot be exact when the oldest sample leaves the window: a seat that sat at NORMAL until run 105, was LOW from 106 and reaches DECOMP at 112 has fallen two bands inside 7 runs, yet a reference that was refreshed at run 111 reads LOW and sees one band. Four band values need only two ages (the run-distance to the last NORMAL and to the last NORMAL-or-LOW), which makes the window exact at its boundary; the review's proposed `band_p_ref` / `ticks_since_drop` pair is replaced by `p_age0` / `p_age1` for that reason.
1006	
1007	**Variables:**
1008	
1009	| Variable | Type | Range | Source | Description |
1010	|---|---|---|---|---|
1011	| `band_p` | enum | NORMAL, LOW, DECOMP, VACUUM | Graph `compartment(cid)`; VACUUM by rule for an EXPOSED seat, NORMAL by rule for an IN_POD seat | the occupant's pressure band, hysteresis inherited (`H_P`); Suit adds none |
1012	| `STAGGER_WINDOW_TICKS` | int ticks | 30-120 (60) | knob | the window, in ticks; `W` is its floor in runs |
1013	| `W` (`STAGGER_WINDOW_RUNS`) | int runs | 5..20 (10) | derived (D.8) | "inside the window" is **inclusive**: a low sample exactly `W` runs old still counts, one of `W` + 1 runs does not |
1014	| `p_age0`, `p_age1` | int runs | 0..`SAT` | `suit.state` (persisted, SE-38) | runs since the index was 0, and since it was 0 or 1; `SAT` means "none inside the window" |
1015	| `cid`, `prev_cid` | int | any compartment id; NONE; POD_CID | Graph `compartment_at`; `prev_cid` is a rebuilt `prev_*` copy | a change of `cid` re-anchors and never fires |
1016	
1017	**Output Range:** at most one `stagger` per fall; `fire` is false on every run in which `cid` changed. A one-band step (0-1, 1-2, 2-3) never fires. A fall of 0 to 2, 0 to 3 or 1 to 3 inside the window fires once on the run the index reaches the lower pressure, and a continuing fall to the next band does not fire again (the consumed ages are `SAT`); a recovery to a lower index and a new fall inside the window is a new event. Cost: two integer compares and two stores per seat per run. **Registry candidate: no (the registry's `stagger` entry already names the trigger by rule, SE-35).**
1018	
1019	**Example 1 (the locked DOOR-BREACH fixture: it does not fire at the default).** `band_p` is NORMAL to step 55, LOW from step 56 and DECOMP from step 143 (D.1). At step 143 the last NORMAL sample is 88 runs old, so `p_age0` has saturated at `SAT` 11 and `fire` is false; VACUUM at step 360 finds the last NORMAL-or-LOW sample 218 runs old: no fire. The breach's stagger comes from the ladder's cap edge (breath CRITICAL, D.3 Example A), not from this trigger. To fire on DOOR-BREACH the window would have to be at least 88 runs = 528 ticks, far outside the knob's range 30-120, so the D.12 trigger is, at the default, a rare-event cue for a decompression that crosses two bands in one second (a hull rupture rather than a door-sized opening); OQ-38 carries the question of whether that is the intended weight. **Example 2 (window boundary, synthetic trace, same compartment).** A sample at index 0 on run `m`, then index 2 on run `m` + 9: `p_age0` 9, fires. On run `m` + 10 (`W`): `p_age0` 10, fires. On run `m` + 11: `p_age0` saturates at 11, no stagger. The same three cases hold for index 1 followed by index 3 with `p_age1`, and at `STAGGER_WINDOW_TICKS` 30 (`W` 5) and 120 (`W` 20) with the boundary at `m` + 5 and `m` + 20. **Example 3 (a crossing).** A seat leaves a NORMAL room (index 0) for a room already at DECOMP (index 2): `cid` changed, the ages re-anchor to `p_age0` `SAT` and `p_age1` `SAT`, no stagger; the breath ladder carries the rest (the reserve engages, SE-4). The same seat standing in that room when its bands fall 0 to 2 inside 10 runs is staggered once. **Example 4 (continuing fall).** Index 0 to 2 on run `n` (fires, ages set to `SAT`), then 3 on run `n` + 3: `p_age1` is `SAT`, no second stagger; had the index recovered to 1 on run `n` + 2 and fallen to 3 on `n` + 3, `p_age1` is 1 and a second event fires.

1021	## Edge Cases

1023	*Each entry is "If [condition]: [exact outcome]. [rationale]" and names the rule or formula it exercises. Step counts are Suit runs (= Graph steps) after a fixture's t = 0.*
1024	
1025	### Respiration, the reserve and the room
1026	
1027	- **If four seats share one compartment and the room holds 450 mGU of O2 on a run in which all four request `R_BREATH`** (SE-5, D.2): the Graph grants in ascending `(compartment id, crew id)`: 300, 150, 0, 0; seats 3 and 4 set `pending_draw_mgu` 300 and debit it from their own reserves one run late (a seat with reserve 0 sets `breath_starved`, which raises its demand to 2 for that run). Suit submits in ascending PlayerId so the order is deterministic; the room is ANOXIC within a run, which switches every seat to RESERVE or NONE, so the lag never persists.
1028	- **If M15 returns its grant synchronously, or only at the next run's phase 0** (SE-5, OQ-12): the ledger is written and consumed in the same run (no lag) or one run later (0.1 s); source selection is identical either way because SE-4 reads only the enums and the reserve. The rule was written to hold under both readings so the Graph's answer cannot change Suit.
1029	- **If a seat requests from a room whose `n_o2` is already 0 on that run** (D.2): granted 0, the full `R_BREATH` is the shortfall, debited from the reserve next run; the Graph's next evaluation reads ANOXIC, so the source is RESERVE (reserve above 0) or NONE (reserve 0) from then on. A seat can therefore lose at most one run of breath to the lag, never a window.
1030	- **If DOOR-BREACH opens on a suited seat with a full reserve** (D.3 Example A): ROOM until step 63, RESERVE with a valve click from step 64 (HYPOXIC with LOW), STRAINED throughout until the reserve crosses `RESERVE_WARN_MGU` at step 663, CRITICAL (stagger, walk-only, warning mark on the strip's breath dial) at step 762, FAILED at step 1113, DEAD at step 1413 unless the room regains air; first cue to FAILED 108.8 s. The decompression itself (DECOMP at step 143, VACUUM at 360) happens inside the reserve, which is the point of buying it.
1031	- **If the same breach hits a seat with reserve 0** (D.3 Example B): GASP from step 64 (the room still holds breathable-in-extremis air in HYPOXIC with LOW), CRITICAL at step 163, NONE from step 116 when the room goes ANOXIC, FAILED at step 313, DEAD at step 613; first cue to FAILED 28.8 s, above `SUIT_MIN_WARNING_S`. A reserve of 0 is the worst case the limiter is sized for.
1032	- **If reserve is 0 in a HYPOXIC room at non-decompressing pressure** (GASP, CK-1): the seat draws from the room and its breath axis holds at CRITICAL (walk-only, the Graph's "stamina loss") for as long as the room stays HYPOXIC, however long that is; FAILED requires ANOXIC, DECOMP or VACUUM. Killing a seat in air the Graph itself calls survivable would break P1; the cost is a long, visible walk-only window and the room's own clock (D.3 Example C: 106 s of GASP on the O2-ROOM fixture).
1033	- **If the room recovers while the seat is in GASP or NONE** (hysteresis `H_P` applies to the enum): the source returns to ROOM on the run the enum is AIR_OK, the demand falls, and the rung follows at once (instant descent, SE-17); the Controller's cap rises on the same run. 1034	- **If `band_o2` flaps between THIN and NORMAL on a hysteresis edge** (SE-19): the demand follows the enum between 1 and 0 with no extra smoothing in Suit; STRAINED has no hold on entry and descent is instant, so the cue tracks the true band and no stagger can result (STRAINED keeps the cap FULL).
