1431	## Game Feel
1432	
1433	*A real note, not a template fill.* Suit has almost no input of its own (one command, `equip_tool`) and no animation; its feel is **the honesty and timing of a body that is running out**. The feel of the walk, the stagger and the work loop belongs to the Controller (PC Game Feel), the feel of how light falls on a rimed shoulder to 2D Lighting, the feel of every sound to Audio; this section owns the numbers underneath them and the one promise Suit makes: **the body is the last instrument that does not lie**, and it speaks slowly enough to be heard and fast enough to be fair.
1434	
1435	**Feel references.** Pandorum's helmet light and breath in a dead corridor for *yours, hands-free, costing something*; Subnautica's oxygen for *a clock the player reads in a number and a sound*; Project Zomboid for *death is a bitch, it happens* (the user's decision), with the difference that here every death is preceded by a tell the player could have read; Don't Starve for *a few honest numbers and a lot of world*. The target is **dry, close and mechanical: a suit, not a hero**. The anti-reference is the health bar with a red vignette.
1436	
1437	**Input responsiveness.**
1438	
1439	| Chain | Steps (ticks at `TICK_RATE` 60) | Budget |
1440	|---|---|---|
1441	| `equip_tool` (press to rail highlight) | the input is sampled in the physics callback before the kernel steps; the Adapter submits the command; validate and apply run at P2 in the same tick; the Presenter plays the hand animation on the **same frame** (the acknowledgement never encodes success) and the rail highlight moves on the committed state at the next presentation frame | at most 1 tick plus 1 render frame (about 17 ms plus one frame) from press to committed `equipped_slot`; no equip time beyond the hand animation (SE-11); no noise |
1442	| `toggle_beam` (press to light) | Suit contributes only the `charge` read in `validate`; the apply is at P2 and the light is committed by `emitter.place` in the same tick | zero Suit latency; at most 1 tick from apply to the lit state the renderer sees (Emitter State Game Feel); the click pre-plays and the light never does |
1443	| Beam off at zero cell | `suit.vitals` drains 6 ticks per run from `emitter.state.lit` as of T-1 and calls `force_off` on the run the cell reaches 0 (P3); `emitter.place` follows in the same tick | the cone is gone the **same tick** as the run that empties the cell; a drain error of at most 5 ticks (0.083 s) per toggle in either direction is accepted and stated |
1444	| A cue after a physical change | the Graph's `graph.propagate.atmo` and `suit.vitals` share offset 2 and divisor 6 *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix)*, so Suit reads the new band enum in the same tick the Graph commits it; the Presenter shows the level at the next presentation frame | at most 6 ticks (0.1 s) of run cadence plus 1 tick plus 1 frame from the physical state change to the on-screen cue; about 117 ms in the worst case |
1445	| Reserve engage (valve click) | the run on which the enums say the air is unbreathable and the reserve is above zero | the click plays on that run's cue edge (the `breath_src_change_seq` edge frame), not before; the closed breath cadence and the strip dial swap follow on the same frame; the fog is not part of this chain *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)* |
1446	| Cap edge to stagger | `locomotion_cap` is committed at P3; `controller.step` follows the same tick | the stagger starts the tick the cap falls (Suit runs before the Controller); `STAGGER_TICKS` 30 (0.5 s) is the Controller's input lock |
1447	
1448	**The ladder as felt time (defaults, all `[PH]`).** The player should feel a body failing in three beats, never one: the first cue (fog level 1, the click, the shorter breath, the shiver and rime) arrives the moment the true state allows; the second beat, the stagger into walk-only with the mark, arrives **at least 10 s** later (`RUNG_MIN_TICKS` 600 ticks) and takes the run away; the third, the collapse, arrives **at least 20 s after the first cue** (`SUIT_MIN_WARNING_S`, itself at least `W_MIN_WARNING_S` 10 s) and starts the Controller's 30 s window (`DOWN_TO_DEATH_TICKS` 1800). Worked on the locked fixtures: DOOR-BREACH with a full reserve is 108.8 s from the first cue to FAILED and with an empty reserve 28.8 s; a suited seat in the O2-ROOM fixture is about 340 s; FREEZE-BREACH is about 10.5 min; a SCORCH room gives 30 s at the minimum. The reserve is 90 s of engaged breath with the warn edge 30 s before empty; the lamp cell is 20 min of lit beam with its warn edge 20 s before dark. **No state is faster than the 20 s floor on an endogenous path**; an exogenous hit (friendly harm, a Horror act) takes its own tell from its own GDD and lands per step, so the victim's rung tracks the harm inside the channel (SE-23).
1449	
1450	**Weight without a number.** Mass never changes speed or noise (SE-28): the Controller's carry state (`V_CARRY` 1 against `V_WALK` 2 and `V_RUN` 3) depends on carrying a module, not on its mass class, and stowed parts change nothing about movement except the one discrete rule of D18 (ruled 2026-10-27, the Controller's): run is disabled while any HEAVY item is stowed, with no grams term *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)*. Weight is **heard**: three breath steps (LIGHT baseline, MEDIUM, HEAVY) where each load step adds *depth, a pack-creak layer and a footfall-linked exhale* and never changes the rate, which belongs to the air class alone (SE-28); thin air is *shallower and faster with no creak*. Provisional audio targets for the spike (`[PH]`, Audio owns the final values): baseline period about 4 s; thin air about 2.5 s (the rate goes up); MEDIUM the baseline period with the breath about 20 % deeper and a 0.6 s creak; HEAVY about 40 % deeper with a 0.9 s creak; the closed reserve cadence about 3 s with a dry rasp; CRITICAL ragged and under 2 s. The test that matters is not the numbers but the **direction** (load: deeper and creaking at the air's own rate; thin: faster and shallower), and it is a blind test (AC-SE-42, at least 90 % correct).
1451	
1452	**What the lamp costs.** The beam is constant until `force_off`: no dim, no flicker, no warm-up, no charge visual in the world. The cost is felt in two places only — the cell whine and the mark at 20 s remaining, then the hard cut into the dark. The cut is the strongest single beat Suit owns, so it is never softened: a fade is a lamp lying about its power, a flicker is the flare's word (`ab:286`). A turn-ON at zero is refused with `CHARGE_EMPTY` and a failed-action cue that does not shake the frame; the lamp stays dark and the glowstick becomes the plan.
1453	
1454	**Impact moments.** (1) *The valve click:* the sound of the reserve taking over, then the sealed, closed cadence and the strip's dial snapping to the reserve — the player learns the click means *the room is no longer breathable* before any tutorial says so. (2) *The first stagger:* a half-second input lock into a walk, no shake, no flash, the run simply gone; the weight of it is the missing speed. (3) *The plate on the back:* picking up the 30 kg hull plate and hearing the breath deepen and the pack creak with the frame appearing on the shoulders — the honest field check. (4) *The cell going out:* a hard cut to black on the chest lamp. (5) *A crewmate's shoulders rimed in your beam,* the one time the player learns the crewmate's temperature without a number. (6) *The DOWNED seat's lamp still burning* while the 30 s window runs. None of these is allowed a screen effect, a stinger or a camera move.
1455	
1456	**Anti-targets.** No health bar and no regeneration; no screen vignette, tunnel, blur, frost edge or damage flash (SE-27); no danger stinger or low-health alarm; no speed buff, no adrenaline, no reduced noise at low vitals (the Controller's rhythm independence); no weight-slowed movement and no inventory screen; no auto-refill of the reserve; no readable body-temperature number; no equip animation that locks the feet; no dimming lamp; no camera shake on any Suit event; no cue that speeds up or slows with sanity.
1457	
1458	**Onboarding: the player learns the vocabulary by living through it, not by dying through it** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review; requirement exported to Derelict Authoring and Boarding & Salvage, OQ-42)*. As specified, nothing guaranteed that a first reserve engagement, a first thin-air breath or a first cold exposure happens where it is survivable, so the cue vocabulary could be learned only by losing up to 20 minutes. Requirement: the authored first sortie must offer, each on a survivable branch and each before any lethal instance of the same hazard, (a) a short unbreathable traverse with breathable rooms at both ends, whose out-and-back time plus the two pod legs stays inside the breath clause of D.11 (at most half of `VACUUM_BUDGET_S` each way: 13 s, about 32 tiles walking, at the defaults; the former `RESERVE_S` / 4 = 22 s each way would have reached CRITICAL on the first sortie once the legs are counted) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*, so the first valve click, fog and closed cadence happen where the exit is reversible; (b) a THIN room that is breathable at its worst; (c) a FROST room with an exit that is not through a lethal strip; and (d) the home-ship O2_TANK port in the starting corridor, so the top-up ritual is met before the first sortie. The cell has a silent advisory step 120 s before the warning (`CELL_ADVISE_S`), so the 20 s warning is never the first the player hears of a 20-minute resource. The proof is AC-SE-92 (a naive-player playtest).
1459	
1460	**Feel acceptance (AC-SE-84 to AC-SE-89)** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review: the six criteria moved to Acceptance Criteria, group H, where the gate table already placed them; the ids are unchanged)*.
1461	
1462	## UI Requirements
1463	
1464	Suit has **no screen of its own**. It supplies true values to three surfaces that the HUD & Suit Layer draws (designed, `hud-and-suit-layer.md`, which repeats this section). The art bible's HUD is a suit worn by the player (`ab §7.0`): a thin reading register on opaque Ground plates, with hue only while the source is alive. Layout, glyph art, numerals and motion are the HUD's and the art-director's; the requirements below say what must be **shown**, **from which value**, **when**, and — as importantly — what must never exist.
1465	
1466	### Surfaces
1467	
1468	| Surface | Contents (all from Suit) | Source value | Notes |
1469	|---|---|---|---|
1470	| **Critical strip** (centre-bottom; capped at 12 % x 5 % of the frame, `ab:751`) | the **breath dial** (arc and numeral, HR-12: the numeral beside the arc) and the breath axis's one warning-mark anchor (the mark sits beside the dial at breath CRITICAL, whichever reading the dial is showing) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* | **while the breath source is RESERVE** the dial shows the **suit O2**, `true_value(suit.reserve, player_id)` (the death clock); **in every other source** it shows the **ambient O2**, `true_value(suit.o2, player_id)` = the **suit-sensed `p_o2` (dkPa) of the occupant's compartment** — the suit's reading of compartment atmosphere, not a Graph overlay (`lsg:51`, `lsg:1000`) | The strip stays inside its cap and swaps the content of one dial; the ambient numeral is demoted to the suit panel while the dial shows the suit O2 (the HUD places it; the art-director confirms the swap fits the strip and HR-3, OQ-41). The numeral is the reading that may lie in Vertical Slice A; the body cue beside it never does. |
1471	| **Suit panel** (bottom-left) | **reserve** (own glyph: the O2 ring clamp with a tank silhouette; the unit is Suit's, delegated ruling R8: a fill fraction in permille of `RESERVE_MAX_MGU`, `reserve_pm` 0..1000, never seconds, because a seconds readout jumps when the leak starts; the HUD chooses only how the fraction is drawn) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*, **integrity**, **warmth** (a zone band in the dial, **no temperature number**), **charge** (cell fill; absent when `CELL_ENABLED` is 0, a dormant configuration at MVP); the warning mark beside the warmth, integrity or charge reading at its CRITICAL (the breath axis's mark is the strip's; the reserve glyph's own mark follows `mark_reserve`, D.10, and is subject to the HUD's merge-or-hide decision, OQ-41 (b)) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)* | `true_value` with keys `suit.reserve`, `suit.integrity`, `suit.warmth`, `suit.charge` | **One mark anchor per axis, plus the ruled reserve mark:** the breath mark sits on the strip's breath dial at breath CRITICAL whatever the breath source (it no longer moves between the reserve glyph and the O2 reading), and `mark_reserve` adds the per-rung mark on the reserve glyph (X9), beside the warmth glyph at warmth CRITICAL, the integrity glyph at integrity CRITICAL, and the charge glyph at `CELL_WARN_S`. Never at STRAINED. |
1472	| **Hand rail** (bottom-right) | the three tool glyphs in slot order (cutter, welder, scanner) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)*; the **equipped** tool in Tungsten fixture colour with the HR-11 bracket; the glowstick count 0-4 as a stick glyph with a number; the carried-module glyph when carrying | `tool_in_hand`, `stowed_count(player_id, cons_glowstick)`, `carried_instance` | The glowstick glyph is Paper White, never Chemlight. Key and button glyphs swap with the active device (the Controller's rule). |
1473	| **Alarm mark** (the HUD places it) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)* | the one-bit ship-alarm mark | `true_value(suit.alarm, player_id)` (TRUTH-class) | Shows while the bit is 1; not rung-based; same beacon phase as the other marks; no text; names no loop or place; it is not an Attention or tell indicator (OQ-37 ruled). |
1474	
1475	### Requirements
1476	
1477	- **UI-1 Wrap point.** The five readings reach the HUD **only** through the Filter's `perceived`, which wraps `true_value(key, player_id)`, keys `suit.o2`, `suit.reserve`, `suit.integrity`, `suit.warmth`, `suit.charge` (and the TRUTH-class bit `suit.alarm`, never lie-capable) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)*, so the Perception Filter has a single wrap point (SE-29). The reading fields of `view(player_id)` (`o2_pp_dkpa`, `reserve_pm`, `cell_pm`, `integrity_pm`) are pre-wrap values for cue derivation and diagnostics; a HUD that draws a number from them is a defect (lint AC-SE-77). The rail count (glowsticks) is an **anchor** with no key (HUD HS-34, Sanity SN-19; OQ-6 closed): the HUD reads it through `stowed_count`, and it is honest at MVP and Vertical Slice A; the suppressant count left the MVP rail (OQ-34) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)*.
1478	- **UI-2 MVP honesty.** Every reading shows the true value in the MVP. Each of the five readings carries the HR-5 tri-modal lie slots (violet fringe gleam, one HR-5 motion signature — glide on a dial needle, continuous tick or stale on a numeral — and sound) as dormant slots so Vertical Slice A can enable a lie without a redraw.
1479	- **UI-3 The mark is rare and rung-based.** The warning mark fires only at CRITICAL on an axis (after the hold) and at `CELL_WARN_S`; at most six at once (the five rung and charge marks plus the `suit.alarm` mark, which is not rung-based), in one beacon phase (2-3 s), never above 3 Hz, solid under reduced motion *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)*. It inherits its reading's class and so is **not** an independent honest backup.
1480	- **UI-4 Update model.** The HUD refreshes a surface when the seat's dirty key `S/<PlayerId>` changes or at render rate, whichever the HUD ADR chooses (→ ADR candidate); a value never animates between two committed values except the dial settle (0.25-0.4 s, overshoot at most 5 %); numerals tick one step per real change.
1481	- **UI-5 Pause, DOWNED, DEAD.** While paused the HUD is frozen and undimmed and `equip_tool` is unavailable (SE-32). While DOWNED the readings keep updating (the seat is still breathing and draining) and the lamp stays lit. A DEAD seat's readings freeze; the restore shows no death screen (SL-8).
1482	- **UI-6 Co-op.** The crew strip carries **no vitals** by default (`ab:902`): a teammate's condition is read by lighting their visor, not from a bar (SE-36). The player's own identity glyph (beam shape plus trim-band count) belongs to the suit panel at Vertical Slice B.
1483	- **UI-7 Accessibility.** Every reading has a numeral or a zone band as well as a hue (colour is redundant with shape and position); the mark is a chamfered square with a stroke, readable in greyscale; reading text meets the HR-12 floors (numerals at least 7 art px cap height, labels at least 5); the UI scale and device glyph settings are anchors that no game state may read or alter (HR-6); under reduced motion the marks hold solid and the dial settle becomes a step. Every body cue has an audio and, where cheap, a visual redundancy (the HEAVY back-frame for the mandatory case); the thin spots (the heat side, the MEDIUM load class) are recorded in Open Questions.
1484	
1485	### What must never exist (anti-requirements)
1486	
1487	No inventory screen, grid or per-part count on any Suit surface (a part count is read by Interaction's repair prompt); **no weight readout** (the mass cue is the breath); **no body-temperature number**; no sanity indicator and no Attention meter on any Suit surface (`ab:741`; the `suit.alarm` mark is a ship-alarm bit, not an Attention meter); no screen-edge tint, vignette or tunnel as a vital indicator (SE-27); no health bar; no banner or toast for a vitals change; no text in Alarm Red (HR-4). Test infrastructure that forces a seat's bands, rungs, cell and reserve for the manual criteria (a debug console owed by the lead-programmer) is **not** a player surface and ships behind the debug flag only.
1488	
1489	> **📌 UX Flag — Suit & Equipment**: this system has UI requirements (the critical-strip O2 reading, the suit panel with the reserve, integrity, warmth and charge readings and their warning marks, and the hand rail with the tools, the glowstick count and the carried-module glyph, and the alarm mark). In Pre-Production, run `/ux-design` for the HUD spec before writing epics; stories should cite `design/ux/hud.md`, not this GDD directly. Noted for the systems index.
